3. every count, coverage, or completeness field — including TOTAL_*, *_COVERAGE, ALL_*, EXPECTED_*, ACTUAL_*, MISSING_*, EXECUTED, SATISFIED, VIOLATED, UNDETERMINED, and RUNS — is an APPLICATION-derived summary under Sections 14.1 and 16.2;
4. every *_RECORDS field is a Section 14.8 projection of its owning Section 38 family, and substantive ownership follows that family's declared partitions;
5. every *_VERSION and *_ID field is an APPLICATION-allocated identity under Section 34.2 or its owning version registry;
6. fields assigned by Sections 14.2, 14.3, and 14.6 follow those assignments;

7. every remaining stage field is an APPLICATION-recomputed summary or immutable reference under Section 14.8; substantive agent or human content never exists as a bare stage field and lives only in its owning family.

A field whose contract is neither explicitly specified nor uniquely produced by these rules is UNDEFINED_FIELD_CONTRACT and blocks specification acceptance; the resolution is a specification change, never an implementation choice.

The same closure governs STAGE_OPERATION_REGISTRY. For every operation: executor class, response permissions, and writable-family constraints come from Section 14.6; required scope from Section 14.7; acceptance mode from Section 17.12; writable families are exactly the Section 38 families whose records the operation's Section 37 description and Section 14.6 contract create or complete, and the Stage 17 and Stage 19 iteration operations reuse the families of their corresponding Stage 10-16 and Stage 15 operations under the new iteration scope; the completion predicate is the owning stage's Section 37 Completion clause; retry behavior is Section 35.6 for exact retries and replacement-prompt regeneration otherwise; independence requirements are exactly those Sections 26.1-26.6 impose on the operation's role. A stage-operation property neither fixed by this specification nor uniquely derivable from these rules is UNDEFINED_OPERATION_CONTRACT and blocks acceptance.

No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.

- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.

- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. Missing, extra, stale, unreserved, or inconsistent dimensions are rejected before proposal creation or command execution.
- preserved failure fixture;
- detection method;
- actual pre-correction execution;
- pre-correction failure result;
- sufficient pre-correction evidence;
- correction;
- distinct later corrected execution;
- post-correction success;
- sufficient post-correction evidence;
- permanent active status unless legitimately retired.
A statement that a test "would have detected" the defect is insufficient.

A failure or regression test is executed only when its target exists and its current EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached. Its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE may not precede target availability. A not-yet-due test remains registered and visible as future work but does not falsely block a prior convergence stage.

Every negative, mutation, adversarial, storage-failure, parser-hostility, and deliberately invalid fixture executes against isolated disposable state: a test-only project clone, test-only IndexedDB namespace, immutable read-only artifact copy, isolated worker input, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must prove that no fixture mutated a canonical user project or an unauthorized third-party target. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.

A regression is ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, or RETIRED. Retirement requires sufficient current evidence that the linked proposition left scope, was replaced so the old mechanism is inapplicable, or the failure mechanism is impossible under the current evidenced architecture; current NOT_APPLICABLE status; required human authorization; independent review; an append-only retirement record; and no current baseline or product dependency. A failing, inconvenient, expensive, unavailable, or flaky regression cannot be retired for that reason. UNKNOWN legitimacy blocks. History is never deleted.

→ obtain one final response JSON file and any required returned files
→ SELECT_RETURNED_FILES by named slot
→ REVIEW_FILE_RESPONSE_PROPOSAL where human review is required
→ accept or reject.

Permanent regressions cover XSS, malicious URLs, malicious filenames, and imported markup.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Every negative, mutation, adversarial, storage-failure, parser-hostility, and deliberately invalid fixture executes against isolated disposable state: a test-only project clone, test-only IndexedDB namespace, immutable read-only artifact copy, isolated worker input, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must prove that no fixture mutated a canonical user project or an unauthorized third-party target. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.
40. Permanent regression obligations
The suite permanently covers these failures:

Every intentional invalid state is created in a disposable project, test-only database namespace, immutable artifact copy, worker-isolated byte set, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must verify both defect detection and absence of mutation to any canonical user project or unauthorized external target.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 45. Browser acceptance
45.1 Actual-iPhone Safari acceptance
- physical-device requirement;
- iPhone model or hardware-class identity as observable;
- exact iOS version and build;
- Safari version and WebKit build identity where observable;
- viewport dimensions and device-pixel ratio;
- storage persistence and quota capability observations;
- canonical HTTPS deployment origin and base path;
- exact deployed commit, deployment-manifest digest, and running build identity;
- test-project identity and initial project package;
- operator or performer identity and identity assurance;
- acceptance procedure version;
- required screenshots, screen recording, exported receipts, logs, and project export;
- unavailable environment facts and their epistemic basis.

The required mobile acceptance executes on an actual iPhone in Safari. Simulator, desktop responsive mode, and another browser are supplementary only and cannot satisfy the physical-device requirement. "Current" is frozen by the target record; a material iOS, Safari/WebKit, application build, origin, storage behavior, or target-device change before final delivery invalidates the affected mobile result and requires revalidation.

The minimum required target-identity tuple is: the physical-device human observation; reported iOS version; observed Safari user-agent string; viewport dimensions and device-pixel ratio; exact deployed commit and deployment-manifest digest; origin; and test-project identity. WebKit build identity and exact hardware model may remain UNKNOWN without blocking; every other tuple member is required.

The only permitted continuations are a new pinned target record on an iOS or Safari version that supports the capability, or a governance change to the controlling specification. No silent degradation path exists.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The current canonical handoff container is a logical manifest plus separately selected exact files. Its identity is the SHA-256 of the canonical manifest, which lists every member by package-relative canonical path, ATTACHMENT_SLOT_ID or outbound role, byte length, hash algorithm, digest, media type, disclosure classification, and requiredness. Member order, file-picker order, download order, and archive order are nonauthoritative.

An optional archive is only a transport representation of the same logical container. It must use the registered deterministic archive profile and pass the archive safety rules. The current profile is closed-loop-archive-profile/1: a ZIP archive containing only STORE (uncompressed) entries, entries ordered by canonical-path unsigned byte order, the UTF-8 filename flag set, every timestamp fixed to 1980-01-01T00:00:00, no directory entries, no symlinks or special entries, no archive comment, no encryption, and no extra fields except a Zip64 field exactly where an entry or archive size requires it. The manifest is always at `manifest.json`; the authoritative prompt is at `instruction.txt`; an inbound response is at `response.json`. Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

The deterministic profile governs application-produced archives only. An inbound archive from an external actor is a nonauthoritative convenience container: it must pass the Section 19.9 safety rules, is exploded into named attachment slots with per-member byte verification, and its original bytes are preserved as evidence. External actors are never required to produce the deterministic profile; the authoritative inbound representation remains response.json plus attachment-slot files.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The current canonical handoff container is a logical manifest plus separately selected exact files. Its identity is the SHA-256 of the canonical manifest, which lists every member by package-relative canonical path, ATTACHMENT_SLOT_ID or outbound role, byte length, hash algorithm, digest, media type, disclosure classification, and requiredness. Member order, file-picker order, download order, and archive order are nonauthoritative.

An optional archive is only a transport representation of the same logical container. It must use the registered deterministic archive profile and pass the archive safety rules. The current profile is closed-loop-archive-profile/1: a ZIP archive containing only STORE (uncompressed) entries, entries ordered by canonical-path unsigned byte order, the UTF-8 filename flag set, every timestamp fixed to 1980-01-01T00:00:00, no directory entries, no symlinks or special entries, no archive comment, no encryption, and no extra fields except a Zip64 field exactly where an entry or archive size requires it. The manifest is always at `manifest.json`; the authoritative prompt is at `instruction.txt`; an inbound response is at `response.json`. Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

WebKit build identity and exact hardware model may remain UNKNOWN without blocking; every other tuple member is required.

The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. Each MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE is single-use: CI accepts at most one evidence file per challenge and rejects reused, unknown, or expired challenges and any evidence bound to a different commit, manifest, origin, target, or test project; a superseding run requires a new challenge. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.

Manifest completeness is established under the same omission-challenge discipline this specification imposes on project content. One extractor drafts the manifest from the controlling text; an independent reviewer that did not receive the draft performs its own extraction or section-by-section coverage pass; a distinct reconciliation resolves every difference; and every specification section is either covered by entries or explicitly recorded as nonnormative with a reason. The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.

entries.controllingText: The application has no controlling service worker unless it is explicitly required, manifested, versioned, security-reviewed, and tested. Clean-profile and previously cached-profile acceptance must load one unmixed build identity or visibly block as stale. The running page, every script and style, and test-worker.js report or are bound to the expected build. Post-deployment verification retrieves every manifest path with cache bypass where supported and rejects missing, extra, redirected-to-different-content, cross-origin, stale, or modified resources. Browser acceptance proves the executed HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and worker resource graph matches the same manifest and build identity; mixed or stale cached builds fail.

46.3 Deployment resource, cache, worker, and supply-chain proof

Before deployment, CI creates closed-loop-deployment-manifest/1 from the audited source commit. It lists canonical origin/base path, source commit, workflow run, build identity, canonicalization and registry identities, build command/environment, workflow-file digest, dependency/lockfile identities, CSP value, and every runtime HTML, JavaScript, CSS, worker, icon, manifest, schema, and asset path with media type, byte length, hash algorithm, and digest. The deployment manifest carries one overall manifest digest computed under closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with the digest field itself omitted; no manifest digest includes itself. Unmanifested runtime resources are prohibited.

entries.controllingText: Field ownership coverage                          = 100%

atomicObligation.statement: The exact deployed commit must prove Field ownership coverage = 100% under the applicable closed metric universe and independently reviewed empty-universe rule.

sourceSpans.text: Field ownership coverage                          = 100%

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Every coverage, completion, agreement, stability, reliability, and zero-count metric publishes:
- metric identity and derivation version;
- the closed universe definition;
- numerator;
- denominator;
- exact included IDs;
- exact excluded IDs and reasons;
- current scope hash;
- evidence references;
- calculated value and disposition.

An empty denominator is SATISFIED only when a current independently reviewed evidence-supported EMPTY_UNIVERSE determination exists for that metric. Otherwise the metric is UNKNOWN or BLOCKED; it is never automatically 100%. A missing trigger record, missing reservation, missing test, or missing proposition cannot make coverage pass by removing itself from the denominator.
49. Definition of done
The exact deployed commit must prove:

Every 100% metric MUST publish its closed universe definition, numerator, denominator, exact included IDs, exact excluded IDs and reasons, derivation identity, and evidence references. An empty denominator passes only when a current independently accepted evidence-supported empty-universe determination exists; otherwise the metric is UNKNOWN or BLOCKED. contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Before accepted semantic intake, every user-supplied file is presumptively required for Stage 01 inspection unless it is mechanically empty, a byte-identical duplicate of an included file, or explicitly excluded by the human through SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT; after accepted intake, later transfer requirements follow Section 29.15 materiality.

File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.

3. every raw input unit is accounted for;

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Each state records its actual evidence and epistemic basis. A package generated or duplicated inside the same IndexedDB origin is not an external backup; browser-local duplicate data in the same origin is not disaster-recovery backup evidence. Production maturity requires a successful restore from the exact exported package bytes.

Before the terminal Stage 30 calculation, the application creates a PRE_DELIVERY_CHECKPOINT bound to the exact Stage 27 through Stage 30 prerequisite records and every authorized artifact byte identity. The checkpoint is exported under the backup policy and its CHECKPOINT_ID is a terminal prerequisite and delivery-record field. The terminal prerequisite is satisfied only when the checkpoint custody state is at least BACKUP_EXPORT_ACTION_COMPLETED; BACKUP_PACKAGE_GENERATED alone is insufficient because an in-origin package is not an external backup. A later post-transfer checkpoint may be recorded but cannot retroactively satisfy preauthorization backup.

The required mobile acceptance executes on an actual iPhone in Safari. Simulator, desktop responsive mode, and another browser are supplementary only and cannot satisfy the physical-device requirement. "Current" is frozen by the target record; a material iOS, Safari/WebKit, application build, origin, storage behavior, or target-device change before final delivery invalidates the affected mobile result and requires revalidation.

The minimum required target-identity tuple is: the physical-device human observation; reported iOS version; observed Safari user-agent string; viewport dimensions and device-pixel ratio; exact deployed commit and deployment-manifest digest; origin; and test-project identity. WebKit build identity and exact hardware model may remain UNKNOWN without blocking; every other tuple member is required.
A failed or incomplete physical-device result blocks final acceptance and release tagging.

Because the canonical handoff container is logical under Section 19.7, per-member sequential export or share on the pinned device satisfies package export whenever a combined multi-file share is unavailable; the optional archive representation is never required. Before the acceptance run, the acceptance procedure executes a recorded MOBILE_CAPABILITY_PROBE on the pinned target covering file export or share, response-file selection, returned-file slot selection, persistent-storage request, logical package export, and backup export and restore. A required capability the pinned target cannot perform yields BLOCKED with the exact missing capability recorded. The only permitted continuations are a new pinned target record on an iOS or Safari version that supports the capability, or a governance change to the controlling specification. No silent degradation path exists.

Before the device run, CI or the authorized acceptance controller creates a cryptographically random MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE of at least 128 bits bound to the exact commit, deployment manifest, origin, target ID, procedure version, and test project. The actual iPhone loads that deployed build and the application records the challenge in its acceptance-mode receipts.

At completion, the application exports `mobile-acceptance-evidence.json` containing the target ID, challenge, build identity, origin, test-project identity, operation receipts, console/runtime findings available to the application, screenshots or recording references, exported project digest, performer identity assurance, physical-device assertion, and evidence basis. CI verifies every mechanically verifiable binding before accepting the record. The physical-device fact remains HUMAN_OBSERVATION or stronger external attestation according to the actual evidence and is never mislabeled application-proven.

The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. Each MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE is single-use: CI accepts at most one evidence file per challenge and rejects reused, unknown, or expired challenges and any evidence bound to a different commit, manifest, origin, target, or test project; a superseding run requires a new challenge. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.

entries.controllingText: An AUTHORIZED terminal determination proves authorization, not physical transfer. Stage 30 therefore exposes the non-stage-increasing terminal action EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS. Immediately before export or share, the application reverifies the exact authorized bytes and current terminal dependency closure, performs the browser-supported export or share action, and records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt in the deliveryAttempts family with its actual evidence basis.

atomicObligation.statement: The application must record a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt in deliveryAttempts with its actual evidence basis.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: After an AUTHORIZED delivery record exists, the current Stage 30 operator action is EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS. It is a non-stage-increasing terminal action. Immediately before export or share, the application revalidates the current delivery record, dependency closure, recipient/destination scope, transfer-count rule, and exact artifact bytes.

The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: PROMPT_INLINE_LIMITS/1 fixes the inline-presentation thresholds: referenced artifact or record content may be embedded inline in the prompt body only up to 65,536 bytes per member and 262,144 aggregate embedded bytes per prompt; beyond either threshold the content MUST travel as manifest-bound attached files or one registered execution package. These limits are centralized, versioned, and acceptance-tested and may be lowered but not raised without a new contract-profile identity.
10.1 Authoritative prompt-file identity

The prompt file does not contain its own bodySha256 or any value whose computation depends on bodySha256. manifest.json carries promptIdentity, including the application-computed bodySha256, and the prompt instructs the external actor to echo the exact manifest promptIdentity. This avoids a self-referential prompt hash.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

Creation of an application-derived receipt, release calculation, evidence-chain calculation, registry calculation, or terminal determination MUST NOT invalidate itself merely because its own atomic commit increments the project revision. Each derived record binds to its precondition dependency closure and committed revision. Only a later mutation affecting that dependency closure makes it stale.
52. Final controlling rule

The terminal evidence hash is computed from the exact Stage 27 release record, Stage 28 identity record and human intent, Stage 29 evidence-chain set and hash, Stage 30 registry calculation, pre-delivery checkpoint, delivery scope, and authorized artifact identities. It is never computed from a summary standing in place of those records.

The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.
52. Final controlling rule

atomicObligation.statement: Completion additionally requires current exact deployed bytes

sourceSpans.text: Completion additionally requires the current exact deployed origin and bytes and the pinned actual physical-iPhone Safari operator path.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The required mobile acceptance executes on an actual iPhone in Safari. Simulator, desktop responsive mode, and another browser are supplementary only and cannot satisfy the physical-device requirement. "Current" is frozen by the target record; a material iOS, Safari/WebKit, application build, origin, storage behavior, or target-device change before final delivery invalidates the affected mobile result and requires revalidation.
A failed or incomplete physical-device result blocks final acceptance and release tagging.

Before the device run, CI or the authorized acceptance controller creates a cryptographically random MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE of at least 128 bits bound to the exact commit, deployment manifest, origin, target ID, procedure version, and test project. The actual iPhone loads that deployed build and the application records the challenge in its acceptance-mode receipts.

At completion, the application exports `mobile-acceptance-evidence.json` containing the target ID, challenge, build identity, origin, test-project identity, operation receipts, console/runtime findings available to the application, screenshots or recording references, exported project digest, performer identity assurance, physical-device assertion, and evidence basis. CI verifies every mechanically verifiable binding before accepting the record. The physical-device fact remains HUMAN_OBSERVATION or stronger external attestation according to the actual evidence and is never mislabeled application-proven.

The evidence file reaches CI through the repository as a committed file or authenticated workflow input from a submitter recorded in the acceptance artifact. Each MOBILE_ACCEPTANCE_CHALLENGE is single-use: CI accepts at most one evidence file per challenge and rejects reused, unknown, or expired challenges and any evidence bound to a different commit, manifest, origin, target, or test project; a superseding run requires a new challenge. The gate minimum for the physical-device fact is HUMAN_OBSERVATION by the recorded performer at the recorded identity assurance; that basis is explicitly sufficient and is never relabeled application-proven.

The deployment manifest binds canonical origin `https://sjonesjones917.github.io`, host `sjonesjones917.github.io`, base path `/closed-loop-tracker/`, the GitHub Pages production environment, a no-cross-origin-redirect policy, and the permitted same-origin runtime-resource set. Deployed verification rejects HTTP downgrade, unexpected host, unexpected custom domain, redirect outside policy, base-path mismatch, cross-origin substitution, or runtime resource outside the authorized deployment root. Identical bytes served from another origin do not satisfy the authorized deployment identity.

Before deployment, CI creates closed-loop-deployment-manifest/1 from the audited source commit. It lists canonical origin/base path, source commit, workflow run, build identity, canonicalization and registry identities, build command/environment, workflow-file digest, dependency/lockfile identities, CSP value, and every runtime HTML, JavaScript, CSS, worker, icon, manifest, schema, and asset path with media type, byte length, hash algorithm, and digest. The deployment manifest carries one overall manifest digest computed under closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with the digest field itself omitted; no manifest digest includes itself. Unmanifested runtime resources are prohibited.

The application has no controlling service worker unless it is explicitly required, manifested, versioned, security-reviewed, and tested. Clean-profile and previously cached-profile acceptance must load one unmixed build identity or visibly block as stale. The running page, every script and style, and test-worker.js report or are bound to the expected build. Post-deployment verification retrieves every manifest path with cache bypass where supported and rejects missing, extra, redirected-to-different-content, cross-origin, stale, or modified resources. Browser acceptance proves the executed HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and worker resource graph matches the same manifest and build identity; mixed or stale cached builds fail.
52. Final controlling rule

entries.controllingText: Completion: Defect and regression histories are append-only; corrections are new records; every confirmed defect has a permanent regression; every due applicable regression execution is current; the pre-delivery checkpoint exists; CALCULATE_TERMINAL atomically creates one AUTHORIZED or BLOCKED delivery determination under Section 36.9. Export or share and any delivery completion are separately receipted and never inferred from authorization. Stage 30 closes through the one atomic CALCULATE_TERMINAL command, which reads the precondition revision, validates registry integrity and all terminal prerequisites, creates exactly one current terminal determination, sets DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED only when every prerequisite is true and otherwise BLOCKED, increments revision once, and commits once. The command's own committed revision does not invalidate its result; only a later revision affecting its dependency closure may supersede or withdraw it. Registry incompleteness blocks Stage 30 unless it proves an earlier premise false; it does not create a Stage 27↔Stage 30 cycle.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The same closure governs STAGE_OPERATION_REGISTRY. For every operation: executor class, response permissions, and writable-family constraints come from Section 14.6; required scope from Section 14.7; acceptance mode from Section 17.12; writable families are exactly the Section 38 families whose records the operation's Section 37 description and Section 14.6 contract create or complete, and the Stage 17 and Stage 19 iteration operations reuse the families of their corresponding Stage 10-16 and Stage 15 operations under the new iteration scope; the completion predicate is the owning stage's Section 37 Completion clause; retry behavior is Section 35.6 for exact retries and replacement-prompt regeneration otherwise; independence requirements are exactly those Sections 26.1-26.6 impose on the operation's role. A stage-operation property neither fixed by this specification nor uniquely derivable from these rules is UNDEFINED_OPERATION_CONTRACT and blocks acceptance.

No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.

- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.

- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The same closure governs STAGE_OPERATION_REGISTRY. For every operation: executor class, response permissions, and writable-family constraints come from Section 14.6; required scope from Section 14.7; acceptance mode from Section 17.12; writable families are exactly the Section 38 families whose records the operation's Section 37 description and Section 14.6 contract create or complete, and the Stage 17 and Stage 19 iteration operations reuse the families of their corresponding Stage 10-16 and Stage 15 operations under the new iteration scope; the completion predicate is the owning stage's Section 37 Completion clause; retry behavior is Section 35.6 for exact retries and replacement-prompt regeneration otherwise; independence requirements are exactly those Sections 26.1-26.6 impose on the operation's role. A stage-operation property neither fixed by this specification nor uniquely derivable from these rules is UNDEFINED_OPERATION_CONTRACT and blocks acceptance.

No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.

- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.

- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. Missing, extra, stale, unreserved, or inconsistent dimensions are rejected before proposal creation or command execution.
- preserved failure fixture;
- detection method;
- actual pre-correction execution;
- pre-correction failure result;
- sufficient pre-correction evidence;
- correction;
- distinct later corrected execution;
- post-correction success;
- sufficient post-correction evidence;
- permanent active status unless legitimately retired.
A statement that a test "would have detected" the defect is insufficient.

A failure or regression test is executed only when its target exists and its current EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached. Its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE may not precede target availability. A not-yet-due test remains registered and visible as future work but does not falsely block a prior convergence stage.

Every negative, mutation, adversarial, storage-failure, parser-hostility, and deliberately invalid fixture executes against isolated disposable state: a test-only project clone, test-only IndexedDB namespace, immutable read-only artifact copy, isolated worker input, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must prove that no fixture mutated a canonical user project or an unauthorized third-party target. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.

A regression is ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, or RETIRED. Retirement requires sufficient current evidence that the linked proposition left scope, was replaced so the old mechanism is inapplicable, or the failure mechanism is impossible under the current evidenced architecture; current NOT_APPLICABLE status; required human authorization; independent review; an append-only retirement record; and no current baseline or product dependency. A failing, inconvenient, expensive, unavailable, or flaky regression cannot be retired for that reason. UNKNOWN legitimacy blocks. History is never deleted.
Stage 27 calculates one current release disposition from the complete due release-evidence universe using this exact precedence:
1. If current sufficient evidence REFUTES any current applicable mandatory proposition, SELECTED_RELEASE_STATE = REJECTED.

2. Otherwise, if any required proposition, applicability, proof obligation, evidence relation, freshness state, independence condition, dependency, due test, artifact, challenge, contradiction, or capability is UNKNOWN, stale, incomplete, insufficient, or blocked, SELECTED_RELEASE_STATE = BLOCKED.
3. Otherwise, if every current applicable mandatory proposition is SATISFIED, SELECTED_RELEASE_STATE = ACCEPTED.
4. No other disposition is valid.

All blockers, contradictions, and unknowns remain recorded even when REJECTED controls. ACCEPTED means PRODUCT_RELEASE_ELIGIBLE only. Release is application-derived and idempotent from a release-evidence hash. Changed dependency-closure evidence supersedes the prior release.

Before Stage 25 inspection, the application executes FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE and creates one application-immutable DELIVERY_CANDIDATE_SET_ID containing the exact artifact IDs, versions, authorized candidate filenames, byte lengths, hashes, transformation records, package membership, parser or viewer requirements, and product lineage. Stage 25 inspects that exact set.

Stage 28 may verify and authorize only the same current DELIVERY_CANDIDATE_SET_ID. Any changed artifact byte, filename, transformation, package membership, viewer-relevant metadata, product lineage, or set membership invalidates Stage 25 and every later terminal result. Byte equality alone cannot substitute for a required representation or package inspection.
Stage 30 uses one idempotent CALCULATE_TERMINAL command. In one transaction it:

A BLOCKED delivery record is a terminal determination record, not an authorization. The command's own committed revision is part of the record and does not invalidate it. Only a later revision that changes a dependency in the recorded terminal dependency closure can supersede, block, or withdraw it. Registry incompleteness blocks Stage 30; it does not mutate Stage 27 into a dependency cycle. A registry finding that objectively refutes an earlier premise invalidates that premise through the responsible-stage map and requires recalculation in order.

RESPONSIBLE_STAGE_MAP is mechanically derived: every canonical family maps to its Section 38 declared stage, and every global family maps to the earliest stage whose gate consumes it; a mutation in a family invalidates from that stage under Section 36.1. Registry findings are classified TERMINAL_ONLY_DEFECT, which blocks Stage 30 only, or PREMISE_REFUTING_DEFECT, which invalidates from the mapped responsible stage. A defect in the release-calculation semantics themselves is an implementation defect handled through the Sections 40-44 regression discipline, never by silently recalculating Stage 27.

The terminal evidence hash is computed from the exact Stage 27 release record, Stage 28 identity record and human intent, Stage 29 evidence-chain set and hash, Stage 30 registry calculation, pre-delivery checkpoint, delivery scope, and authorized artifact identities. It is never computed from a summary standing in place of those records.

The application records a DELIVERY_ATTEMPT receipt containing the delivery ID, attempt ID, exact artifacts, byte hashes, operator action, intended recipient/destination/channel, device-reported time, result, and available external receipt. When the requested outcome includes delivery to the operator or another destination, Stage 30 workflow completion requires at least one successful authorized export or share attempt within the delivery record's scope. DELIVERY_STATE = AUTHORIZED permits the UI to say "Delivery authorized." It may say "Delivery attempted" only after the action receipt exists. It may say "Delivered" only when current evidence attributable to the recipient, destination, channel, or external system establishes transfer at its actual epistemic basis. The application cannot prevent or count transfers performed outside its controlled action path and must display that limitation. It does not claim it can undo a completed external transfer.

Creation of an application-derived receipt, release calculation, evidence-chain calculation, registry calculation, or terminal determination MUST NOT invalidate itself merely because its own atomic commit increments the project revision. Each derived record binds to its precondition dependency closure and committed revision. Only a later mutation affecting that dependency closure makes it stale.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Before accepted semantic intake, every user-supplied file is presumptively required for Stage 01 inspection unless it is mechanically empty, a byte-identical duplicate of an included file, or explicitly excluded by the human through SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT; after accepted intake, later transfer requirements follow Section 29.15 materiality.

File-inspection status is the closed set INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF, which the application establishes; EXTERNAL_INSPECTION_CLAIMED, which is agent-asserted; INSPECTION_SUPPORTED, which is the claim plus complete consistent per-unit dispositions and source locations; and INSPECTION_ESTABLISHED_TO_REQUIRED_BASIS, which is the minimum basis the file's contract requires. Stage 01 completion requires INCLUDED_IN_HANDOFF as an application fact and at least INSPECTION_SUPPORTED for every required file; the word inspected always means at the recorded basis and is never represented as an application-proven semantic fact. A required artifact whose semantic content is INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED and not proven immaterial leaves Stage 01 BLOCKED unless human authority removes it from project scope through a new input version.
7.6 Stage 01 completion
Stage 01 completes only when:

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The application derives DUE_NOW only when the current stage is at least EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, the target-availability condition is TRUE, the obligation is current and applicable, and the current stage is at or beyond its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. UNKNOWN target availability blocks only when the obligation could be due.

Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 evaluate only current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligations whose PER_RUN_REQUIRED value is TRUE and that are due by the relevant stage. Final-product, representation, delivery, evidence-closure, registry-closure, and terminal-delivery obligations do not block Stage 18 or Stage 19 before their targets exist, and Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 MUST NOT require product-only, representation-only, delivery-only, or terminal-only propositions before their targets exist. They remain preserved as future required obligations and become due at their declared stages.
31. Ten-run stability and reliability metrics

A run execution attempt that ends REJECTED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED never counts toward the exactly-ten requirement and cannot satisfy any matrix cell. Its reservation reaches a terminal state, the same run target slot is re-reserved under Section 35.6, and the replacement attempt receives a new fresh context reserved for that run. The superseded context becomes historical, is excluded from the ten-distinct-context calculation, and its outputs cannot appear in any authorized input. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. An accepted run is never re-executed within the same iteration; a defect discovered in an accepted run routes through Stages 13-17.

Completion: The complete current required relation set exists for every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED proposition, run, and test. Every verifier satisfies the semantic-review independence contract. Every required tuple has sufficient evidence and exactly one valid determination; no nondue or meaningless Cartesian cell is manufactured.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.
